\section{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Sharp --- Finite Noise Optimization}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Sharp.FiniteNoiseOptimization
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Sharp --- Finite Noise Optimization: Introduction}
Optimization on a weighted moment sphere produces nonnegative extremizers. Differentiation and strict concavity show that these extremizers have at most two distinct coordinate values.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Sharp --- Finite Noise Optimization: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Compactness of a weighted moment sphere]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_moment_sphere_compact}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, let $w_i>0$ for every $i	extrm{ in }I$, and let $p>0$. The set of
vectors $f:I\to\bbr$ satisfying $\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p=1$ is compact in the usual
finite-dimensional topology.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two values on a strict-concavity level set]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_concave_level_two_values}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be finite, let $\varphi:\bbr\to\bbr$ be strictly concave on $[0,\infty)$, and let
$f:I\to\bbr$ be nonnegative. If there is a real number $c$ such that $\varphi(f_i)=c$ for
every $i	extrm{ in }I$, then there are $a,b
earrow0$ such that each $f_i$ equals either $a$ or $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of weighted forms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_homogeneity}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, let $w:I\to\bbr$, let $p,\rho,t
e\in\bbr$, and let $f:I\to\bbr$. Define $G(g)=\sum_iw_i|g_i|^p$ and
$F(g)=\rho^2\sum_iw_ig_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_ig_i)^2$. Then $G(tf)=|t|^pG(f)$ and
$F(tf)=t^2F(f)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative condition at a quotient maximum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.derivative_eq_mul_of_isLocalMax_quotient}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $x,r,a,b\in\mathbb{R}$. Suppose $f$ is
differentiable at $x$ with derivative $a$, $g$ is differentiable at $x$ with derivative
$b$, $g(x)=1$, and $t\mapsto f(t)/g(t)^r$ has a local maximum at $x$. Then $a=r f(x)b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Normalization of weighted forms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_normalization}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_homogeneity}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $w_i,p,\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ with $p\ne0$, and let
$f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $G(f)>0$, where $G(h)=\sum_iw_i|h_i|^p$ and
$F(h)=\rho^2\sum_iw_i h_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_i h_i)^2$. Set $c=G(f)^{-1/p}$. Then
$G(cf)=1$ and $F(cf)=F(f)/G(f)^{2/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_directional_derivatives}

Let $I$ be finite, let $w:I\to\bbr$, let $p>1$ and $\rho
e\in\bbr$, and let $g,h:I\to\bbr$ with $g_i
earrow0$ for every $i$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and
$F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. At $t=0$, the derivative of
$G(g+th)$ is $p\sum_iw_ig_i^{p-1}h_i$, and the derivative of $F(g+th)$ is

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stationarity of a noise maximizer]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_maximizer_stationarity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.derivative_eq_mul_of_isLocalMax_quotient, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_directional_derivatives, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_normalization}
\difficulty{6}
Let $I$ be a finite set with weights $w_i>0$ and $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $1<p<2$ and
$0\le\rho<1$. For $h:I\to\mathbb{R}$, define $G(h)=\sum_iw_i|h_i|^p$ and
$F(h)=\rho^2\sum_iw_i h_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_i h_i)^2$. Suppose $g_i\ge0$ for every
$i$, $G(g)=1$, and $F(f)\le F(g)$ for every $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ with $G(f)=1$. Then
$F(g)\ge1$ and, for every $i$, $F(g)g_i^{p-1}-\rho^2g_i=(1-\rho^2)\sum_jw_jg_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two values at a noise maximizer]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_maximizer_two_values}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_concave_level_two_values, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_maximizer_stationarity}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite set with weights $w_i>0$ and $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $1<p<2$ and
$0\le\rho<1$. For $h:I\to\mathbb{R}$, define $G(h)=\sum_iw_i|h_i|^p$ and
$F(h)=\rho^2\sum_iw_i h_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_i h_i)^2$. Suppose $g_i\ge0$ for every
$i$, $G(g)=1$, and $F(f)\le F(g)$ for every $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ with $G(f)=1$. Then there
exist $a,b\ge0$ such that every value of $g$ is either $a$ or $b$.
\end{theorem}
